original.quote:
Consider a finite alphabet $\mathcal A$ and a process law $P$ on $\mathcal A^{\mathbb N_0}$; $H_n:=H(X_0^{n-1})$ is as in [[def-finite-block-information-and-entropy]].

Define the upper information rate $\overline h(P):=\limsup_{n\to\infty}H_n/n$ and, when the limsup and liminf agree, the information rate $h(P):=\lim_{n\to\infty}H_n/n$. This definition does not assume stationarity.

Since $X_0^{n-1}$ has at most $|\mathcal A|^n$ values, $0\le H_n\le n\log_2|\mathcal A|$; consequently both rates are defined and lie in $[0,\log_2|\mathcal A|]$.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. All functions below have domain $X$. Let $f$ and $(f_n)$ be measurable complex-valued functions such that
$f_n\to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for a single
nonnegative measurable function $g$ with $\int g\,d\mu<+\infty$. Then
$f\in L^1(\mu)$,
$$\int|f_n-f|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0,$$
and hence
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\longrightarrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

original.quote:
Consider a finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal A$, a probability measure $P$ on $\mathcal A^{\mathbb Z}$, and the left shift $T(x)_j=x_{j+1}$.

The shift is measurable on the product sigma-algebra. Call $P$ stationary when it is measure preserving under this shift, precisely the condition in [[def-measure-preserving-transformation-and-system]].

For a stationary $P$, call the source ergodic when each event $E$ satisfying $T^{-1}E=E$ has $P(E)\in\{0,1\}$; by [[def-ergodic-measure-preserving-system]] this is exactly ergodicity of the probability system.

original.claim: Every dictionary entry is an ordinary word over $\mathcal A$. As long as unread text remains it ends in $\#$, so no dictionary word can consume the entire unread text. The root is always a prefix, and there are finitely many entries; hence a longest match and a following symbol exist. Every iteration removes at least one symbol from a finite string, so the parser terminates at its final marker record.

If an ordinary phrase $wc$ were already a dictionary entry, it would be a longer prefix of the unread text than the selected $w$, contradicting the longest-prefix rule. Thus each ordinary phrase is new, and ordinary inserted phrases are distinct. The terminal phrase contains the new symbol $\#$ and is different from every ordinary phrase.

proposed.quote:
An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].
